title: Where he got the most recognition; preferring sideman work to leading
summary: Stewart names Tatum, Slim Gaillard, the Goodman sextet and his own Garner quartet; he disliked leading because of friction in his quartet with Beryl Booker, Collins and West.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well, now, when you -- which of the bands that you were working with did you think that you began to get the most attention playing?
Any groups that you were with, small or large.

I think -- yes, right. I think that my best experience, as far as recognition, was working with Art Tatum and, of course, I might also add, Slim Gaillard (PHONETIC), when we had our duo, and let's go a little further, and say that I got quite a bit of recognition working with Benny Goodman, the Benny Goodman Sextet. Outside of that, let's not forget when I had my own quartet with Erroll Garner.
Did you prefer working as a side man to being a leader?

Well, I was just as happy working as a side man rather than being a leader because I had found that being a leader is quite a bit of pressure involved and at times, you don't -- you really don't want to go through some of the hassles that are involved sometimes. I have been a

leader, I'd say on a couple of occasions, when I had a couple of groups. It wasn't too bad, but there were times that you have to study the situation real hard in order to get along with your co-workers and what have you, at times, even musically.
Well, do you remember which times those were, when you had to work the hardest at getting along with the guys and making the music work?

Well, I would -- let's see if I can remember. One time, after Billy Taylor was with me for a while on piano, after Billy left, I had a young lady to play piano with me. Her name was Beryl Booker and of course, let's see, I had a quartet at that particular time with Johnny Collins on the guitar and Harold West on the drums and of course, there were times when we -- there were little situations where they used to argue amongst themselves, you know, and I tried to get them straight, cool things and what have you. But at times, there was a bit of responsibility in order to keep harmony in the group.
That was one of the times when I'd rather not have been a leader, you know.
Oh, because of trying to keep the people in the band --
Happiness in the family, you know,
So that's why you chose to not keep leading bands?
